subtitle: Warm or cold words, and durchaus, keineswegs, geradezu
words.intro: When you leave a German job you’re entitled to a written reference. By law, it has to be kind. So a whole secret language has grown up in which each kind word is a verdict. *Er war stets bemüht* means he tried, always, and never managed it.

grammar[0].subheading: Warm, neutral and cold; and the language of public life
grammar[0].blocks[1].title: Which word do you choose?
grammar[0].blocks[2].note: A text that uses these has taken a side without an opinion sentence.
grammar[0].fact: A company never fires anyone: it *setzt frei*, sets them free. A price is *angepasst*, adjusted. Each year a German jury picks an *Unwort des Jahres*, the most misleading word in public use. *Sozialverträgliches Frühableben* has held a place in the hall of shame.

grammar[1].subheading: From a strong no to a strong yes, and false friends
grammar[1].blocks[1].title: durchaus: yes or no?
grammar[1].blocks[2].title: Watch these
grammar[1].fact: *Durchaus* looks as though it means *throughout*, and it doesn’t. *Das ist durchaus möglich* means that it certainly is possible, whatever you may think. *Keineswegs* is a very firm no, in a very good suit.

document.intro: A real reference from a cotton mill, signed in 1859, and it’s a single sentence. Adam Hofmann had worked there for fifteen years. Before the codes and the lawyers, three adjectives were enough: *treu, fleißig und ordentlich*.
document.fact: German workers once carried an *Arbeitsbuch*, in which each employer wrote his remarks. So your whole working life went with you.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Say each thing in a cold word.
reading.intro: Jonas is leaving the press office. Frau Prof. Lange has signed his reference. He’s delighted. Lena, who has worked in personnel, is already looking worried.
reading.fact: German law really does require a reference to be *wohlwollend*, benevolent, and clear, and hidden codes are officially banned. It doesn’t stop them. It’s common for bosses to ask staff to draft their own.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Draw a line from each phrase to what it really means.
